title: Angle reasons card
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lessons 63, 64 (Angle reasons card (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: To understand how to use the facts about angles on a straight line and around a point to find missing angles

questions.q: Angles x, 48° and 75° lie on a straight line. Find x and give the reason.
questions.a: x = 57°: angles on a straight line add up to 180°
questions.model: 48 + 75 = 123. 180 - 123 = 57, so x = 57° (angles on a straight line add up to 180°).

questions.q: Four angles meet at a point: 100°, 85°, 95° and a. Find a.
Angles 4x and 2x lie on a straight line. Find x.
Two lines cross. One angle is 3x and the angle opposite it is 84°. Find x.
questions.model: Vertically opposite angles are equal: 3x = 84. x = 84 ÷ 3 = 28.

questions.q: Two lines cross at 90°. Find all four angles.
Opposite angles are (2x + 10)° and (x + 50)°. Find x.
Find each lettered angle, giving reasons: (a) 132° and a on a straight line (b) 110°, 70°, 90° and b at a point (c) 3c and 45° on a straight line (d) d, d, d and 120° at a point
questions.model: (a) a = 180 - 132 = 48°, because angles on a straight line add up to 180°. (d) 3d + 120 = 360, 3d = 240, d = 80° (angles at a point add up to 360°).

questions.q: Angles (x + 20)°, (2x - 10)° and 2x° lie on a straight line. Find each angle.
Five angles at a point are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : 5. Find the largest.

Find the lettered angles, giving a reason each time: (a) lines cross with one angle 58°: find a (opposite) and b and c (neighbours) (b) opposite angles are 5y and 135° (c) angles (4p - 20)° and (2p + 40)° are vertically opposite: find p and the angle
questions.model: (a) a = 58° (vertically opposite angles are equal). b = 180 - 58 = 122° (angles on a straight line); c = 122° (vertically opposite b).

questions.q: Three straight lines cross at one point, making six angles. Two neighbouring angles are 50° and 70°. Find the other four.
Write a full proof, with a reason on each line, that vertically opposite angles are equal.
questions.a: a + b = 180° and b + c = 180° (angles on a straight line), so a + b = b + c and a = c.

questions.q: Angles on a straight line add up to:
125° and y lie on a straight line. y?
Big question: why must angles on a straight line add up to 180°?
questions.a: A straight line is half a full turn, and a full turn is 360°.

questions.q: One angle at a crossing is 33°. Its neighbour?
Big question: why are vertically opposite angles always equal?
questions.a: Each one makes 180° with the same neighbour, so both equal 180° minus that neighbour.
